findings.text: Diagnostic dump operating on a virtual CPU is visible outside its file and reports guest host and control state by reading virtual machine control fields and emitting log lines, with no effect on control flow beyond logging.

Register write handling for conventional virtualization and for trust domain guests plus the predicate describing which registers trust domains emulate are visible outside their files and use a small status distinguishing accepted writes from rejected ones.

The technology layer selects behavior by guest flavor, using trust domain handling for trust domain virtual CPUs and conventional extensions handling otherwise, for both the query about unhandleable emulation need and the register write path.

Page modification log draining follows a short lifecycle with empty detection followed by overflow aware tail derivation followed by ordered dirty marking followed by index reset, leaving the log ready for fresh hardware entries.

When the log holds entries the drain walks from the head downward toward the computed tail so dirty marking follows hardware write order, expects page aligned guest addresses, converts each address to a page number for dirty tracking, and restores the index to its initial head value afterward.

Nested cleanup marks three cached host mappings dirty when present, covering access page plus virtual APIC plus posted interrupt descriptor state, delegating presence testing and per page dirty marking to shared helpers.

A host mapping record exposes a host address field whose nonzero value denotes a valid mapping and a guest frame field used for dirty tracking when valid, with validity tested by simple nonzero check and dirty marking conditioned on validity.

Dumping is gated by an enable flag that causes early return with a rate limited notice when disabled, otherwise it reads execution controls and guest host and control fields conditionally on processor capabilities and formats selectors plus descriptor tables plus register lists through small helpers.

Effective extended feature reporting during dump prefers the loaded control value when entry controls request loading, else the autoload table entry when present, else a host maintained value adjusted for long mode bits according to whether entry controls request 64 bit mode.

Exception information address obtained from controls may be corrupt when dumping after a failure, so the implementation avoids dereferencing that address and instead uses a known virtual address while noting a mismatch against the expected physical address.

Unexpected conditions are reported without aborting the current operation, including misaligned logged addresses during dirty marking and an unexpected emulation flag on trust domain guests which is checked only once.

Trust domain register writes first apply dedicated extended machine check control validation involving host origin plus capability advertisement plus reserved bit checks, then reject a tiny read only set, then reject registers outside the emulated set, then delegate remaining emulated registers to common handling.

Trust domain emulation covers MSR_KVM_POLL_CONTROL as well as MSR_IA32_MCG_STATUS in addition to MSR_PLATFORM_INFO together with MSR_MTRRdefType alongside MSR_IA32_UCODE_REV as well as MSR_IA32_TSC_DEADLINE in addition to MSR_IA32_CR_PAT together with MSR_MTRRcap alongside a contiguous memory type range ending at the fixed 4K region as well as MSR_IA32_POWER_CTL in addition to MSR_IA32_ARCH_CAPABILITIES together with MSR_MISC_FEATURES_ENABLES alongside MSR_IA32_MISC_ENABLE as well as MSR_IA32_MCG_CAP in addition to MSR_IA32_MCG_CTL together with MSR_IA32_MCG_EXT_CTL alongside machine check bank controls and second level bank controls as well as MSR_IA32_APICBASE in addition to MSR_EFER together with MSR_IA32_FEAT_CTL alongside an extended interrupt subset described separately. A narrower read only subset is limited to three members from that larger set.

Extended interrupt emulation spans APIC_TMCCT as well as APIC_ESR in addition to APIC_LVTERR together with APIC_TMICT alongside APIC_LVT0 as well as APIC_TDCR in addition to APIC_LVR together with APIC_ICR alongside APIC_LVTT as well as APIC_SPIV in addition to APIC_LDR together with APIC_LVTCMCI alongside APIC_LVTTHMR as well as APIC_LVTPC in addition to APIC_ID together with APIC_LVT1, excluding entries that hardware virtualizes and the host cannot emulate.

Conventional register writes dispatch by register identity with per register acceptance rules involving guest capability advertisement plus host origin privilege plus canonical address form plus reserved bit clearance plus nested mode plus tracing capability, mirroring selected values into nested copies when nested and applying side effects such as cache clearing plus interception relaxation plus bitmap maintenance plus event creation plus tracing updates.

When running nested, system entry registers plus debug control plus bound configuration plus pattern type are stored both to hardware controls and to nested control copies, with entry addresses truncated to guest width and debug plus bound plus pattern copies conditioned on relevant save or load controls, while feature control clearing from host exits nesting and tracing writes update intercept state.

Rejected writes use a distinct nonzero status that asks the caller to fail the guest operation, applied to unsupported features plus malformed values plus guest attempts on host only or read only registers plus tracing writes without required capabilities or while nested virtualization is active.
